payload.blocks: ACE phase 3 and ASC phase 3: both run fgos authority declare --kind component, which needs an answered owner question as --approved-by.
payload.headline: Approve one id for the two new component declarations (agent-context-engine and agent-start-context)?

parts.cause: Checked fgos authority declare --help and the planner report Q1: --approved-by takes the id of an answered question; a supervisor event id or a chat answer does not count.

options.does: This one question, once answered, is the approval id for both declarations.
options.harm: The id names two components, so a later reader must read both plans to see the scope.
options.label: One question for both

options.does: Ask one question per component and answer each.
options.gain: Each approval names exactly one component.
options.harm: A second owner round-trip for the same decision.
options.label: Two separate questions

options.cost: A door change in Rust plus its tests and a decision.
options.does: Let the door accept a decided-in-chat marker instead of a question id.
options.harm: Widens the door; the repo rules say to make contracts tighter, not larger.
options.label: Add a waiver to the declare door

parts.recommendation: One question for both. It costs one answer and changes no code. The owner already chose this option in chat on 2026-11-25; the answer here only records it in the store.

scope.allows: The two declarations only: component agent-context-engine and component agent-start-context.
scope.forbids: Any other new component, decision kind or door, and any change to the declare door itself.

parts.what: Plans agent-context-engine and agent-start-context each declare one new component in the authority model. The declare door refuses a new component without an answered owner question naming it. The two decisions (ACE-D3 and ASC-D1) were settled in chat and relayed as an event, but neither is a question in the store.
